doc_friction.issue: einvoice-preflight is listed at 40.4 s, but alone it takes 9.3 s; times taken 4-suites-parallel mislead about which suites are worth a perf run, and I spent a run of the suite finding that out.
Foreground sleep is blocked and Monitor needs a ToolSearch load first; waiting on a background test run took several attempts. An until-loop in a foreground Bash call with a timeout worked.

deviations.why: Both perf backlog items (P063, P064) are owner-gated CODEOWNERS paths.
deviations.did: Skipped the pool reading (item 2) and went to the slowest local suite (item 3), changepoint-detector.
deviations.result: Found a 3.5x call redundancy in the stale-feed fit; the affected files run 1.9x faster.

notes: Metric: wall and user CPU of the 27 changepoint-detector test files that import update-rate or the stale-feed tests, all run in one node --test (default concurrency, 4 cores), old files swapped in vs new: 32.6 s -> 17.1 s wall, 83.6 s -> 50.6 s user, 141/141 pass both. One test, 'a stale feed that was fixed' (update-rate.test.mjs) alone: 13.1 s -> 4.6 s (time node --test --test-name-pattern). Cause: roundedWalkLogLik 10,640 calls / 3,040 distinct, Markov 13,680 / 4,560 (counted by instrumenting). watch CLI --suggest call (closed-days test): 6.15 -> 5.41 s from the PELT pruning reuse. Equivalence: partitionRates old vs new on 18,000 random inputs (exact and grid paths) JSON-identical; staleLRMarkov / staleLikelihoodRatio / heavy on 59 random fits identical in every field. Full suite: python3 platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py changepoint-detector ok, 1,007 tests, 176.7 s (baseline whole suite 188.7 s wall, but that baseline overlapped my first edit, so it is not a clean before; the suite wall is set by engine files this change does not touch). Also read: einvoice-preflight 9.3 s alone, ai-bookkeeper 23.2 s alone, so neither is worth a perf run now.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: profiling, call counting, two equivalence harnesses, A/B timing and write-up for a senior engineer

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
